chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man entered with a group in their prayer while he did not intend it as a prayer. Then their Imam had a nullification (hadath), so he took the hand of that man, brought him forward, and led them in prayer. Does their prayer suffice for them by his prayer while he did not intend it as a prayer? He said: 'It is not fitting for a man to enter with a group in their prayer while he does not intend it as a prayer. Rather, it is fitting for him to intend it as a prayer. If he has already prayed, then he has another prayer; otherwise, let him not enter with them. Their prayer suffices for the group even if he did not intend it.'

If the one who steps forward as a deputy for the Imam has missed one or two rak'ahs of the prayer, let him complete the prayer with them, then let him lead them in prayer (imam), so that will be their departure from the prayer, and he will complete what remained of it for himself. He narrated that.

key_terms.يَنْوِيهَا صَلَاةً: Intends it as a prayer (intention of prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an Imam leads the prayer but did not intend to pray personally?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the fiqh of 'intention' (niyyah) in congregational prayer, specifically addressing a scenario where a follower leads after the Imam's prayer is nullified. It establishes that validity for the congregation depends on the leader's intention to pray, while also detailing the procedural nuance for a deputy Imam who has missed rak'ahs, requiring him to complete the prayer with the congregation before performing the remaining units individually. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal state of the worshipper alongside the external act of leading.
